; -*- mode: Org;-*-

* Goal
      Make the arm64 devbox tarball (arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz) SAFE to
      extract at "/" on a provisioned host, so installing it never breaks
      the host's SSH login.

      Concrete deliverable: a rebuilt arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz whose
      member list contains NONE of the host-identity / host-login files
      that clobbered a live Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 ECS box during
      (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/install.arm64.sh" 1).

      Root cause (already diagnosed on the reimaged box):
      - The tarball is extracted with `tar zxf ... -C /`, and it SHIPS the
        build container's SSH server config + host identity, which overwrite
        the host versions:
        - etc/ssh/sshd_config  -> wipes the cloud login hook
              `AuthorizedKeysCommand /usr/bin/ecs_config_instance_connect --uid %U`
              and the explicit `PasswordAuthentication yes` / `PermitRootLogin yes`
              → both password AND cloud-injected key auth stop working.
        - etc/ssh/ssh_host_*   -> replaces host keys with the image's baked-in
              keys (root@buildkitsandbox), causing REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION
              CHANGED on every client + identical keys across all boxes.
        - etc/pam.d/sshd       -> container PAM stack can conflict with host.
        NOTE: architecture was NOT the cause — every shipped binary is correct
        aarch64.

      DECISION (operator, 2026-07-27): KEEP root/.ssh/* in the tarball.
      - root/.ssh/authorized_keys + root/.ssh/config are considered safe to
        ship (they are the operator's own dev key + a github ProxyCommand
        convenience config, not part of the host's SSH-server identity).
      - BUT a raw `tar -C /` still OVERWRITES /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.
        Evidence: tarball key = bartuer@bartuers-MacBook (SHA256:5SGHkP…)
        vs host key = bazhou@nixbase2 (SHA256:tfMXq7…) — DIFFERENT. A plain
        extract drops the host's own key. So the fix for root/.ssh is
        APPEND-not-overwrite at install time, NOT removal from the tarball.

      Success criteria:
      - [X] `tar tzf arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz` contains NO etc/ssh/sshd_config
      - [X] ...contains NO etc/ssh/ssh_host_* (private or public host keys)
      - [X] ...contains NO etc/ssh/ssh_config
      - [X] ...contains NO etc/ssh/moduli
      - [X] ...contains NO etc/pam.d/sshd
      - [X] root/.ssh/authorized_keys is NOT shipped directly; it ships as the
            STAGING file root/.ssh/authorized_keys.devbox. (root/.ssh/config was
            DROPPED entirely — operator decision — since the container gets it
            from the IMAGE and the host has a richer one to preserve.)
      - [X] install.arm64.sh APPENDS (dedup) the shipped authorized_keys.devbox to
            any pre-existing /root/.ssh/authorized_keys instead of overwriting it
      - [X] Still contains the intended payload: sshd, ssh, scp, sftp,
            git + HTTPS closure, ca-certificates, /bin/entry, /root/.bashrc
      - [X] Extracting the new tarball on the LIVE host preserved a working
            sshd_config (cloud AuthorizedKeysCommand + PasswordAuthentication intact)
            and preserved the pre-existing operator key in authorized_keys
            (verified on this host: 2 keys, host fp unchanged, sshd -t OK).

* Dependencies
      - Packer that builds the tarball (THE fix target):
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/pack.base.arm64.sh" 1)
      - Legacy packer with the same defect (keep in sync or delete):
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/pack.arm64.sh" 1)
      - Build image definition (COPYs authorized_keys/config into image):
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/Dockerfile.base" 1)
      - Installer that extracts at / on the host:
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/install.arm64.sh" 1)
      - Runtime entrypoint (already generates host keys at container start):
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/entry.sh" 1)
      - The offending artifact to re-inspect after rebuild:
            /root/arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz  (18M, 709 members — reference copy)
      - Docker engine — REQUIRED to REBUILD the tarball. Status on this box:
        INSTALLED 2026-07-27 (Docker CE 29.6.2, buildx v0.35.0, daemon active).
        `docker run --rm ubuntu:24.04 uname -m` → aarch64 (native, no qemu).
      - Host arch check: `uname -m` = aarch64 == target arm64 (folder name
        …-arm64). Therefore BUILD NATIVELY — plain `docker build`, NOT
        `buildx --platform` + qemu. New native driver:
            (link "/root/local/src/dot-emacs/build/devbox-ubuntu-24.04-arm64/build.base.native.sh" 1)
        (build.macos.sh remains the CROSS-build path for x86_64 hosts.)
      - Verification is docker-free: the acceptance oracle + compare_devbox_tar.sh
        need only tar/grep/sort (all present). Only the REBUILD needs docker.

* Context
      Why the ship-SSH-config approach existed and why it must change:
      - The packer's intent is to deliver a runnable openssh-server so the
        container can be SSH'd into. That is legitimate for a FRESH docker
        image, but FATAL when the same tarball is unpacked over a running,
        cloud-provisioned host that already owns /etc/ssh.
      - entry.sh ALREADY does `ssh-keygen -A` and creates the sshd privsep
        user at container start, so shipping host keys / server config in the
        tarball is redundant even for the container use case.

      The offending list-builder in pack.base.arm64.sh:
      - `find /etc/ssh`  → drags in sshd_config, ssh_config, ssh_host_* AND moduli
      - `dpkg -L openssh-server` → drags in /etc/ssh/sshd_config + /etc/pam.d/sshd
      - explicit `printf ... /root/.ssh/config /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` → KEEP
        (operator decision — these two stay in the tarball).

      Fix strategy (remove SERVER identity from tarball; KEEP root/.ssh;
      make root/.ssh install append-safe):
      - Replace `find /etc/ssh` with an EXPLICIT allowlist that excludes the
        server config and every host key:
            find /etc/ssh -type f ! -name 'sshd_config' ! -name 'ssh_config' \
              ! -name 'ssh_host_*' ! -name 'moduli'
        (moduli is regenerable; excluding it avoids clobber.)
      - Add a post-filter (grep -v) as defence-in-depth AFTER list.final is
        built, so a future dpkg -L that re-introduces server paths is stripped
        — but DO NOT strip root/.ssh (kept by design):
            grep -vE '^etc/ssh/(sshd_config|ssh_config|moduli)$' \
          |  grep -vE '^etc/ssh/ssh_host_' \
          |  grep -vE '^etc/pam\.d/sshd$'
      - KEEP the explicit `/root/.ssh/config /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` lines.
      - CRITICAL: because `tar -C /` OVERWRITES /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and
        the shipped key (bartuer@…) differs from a host key (bazhou@…), the
        install step must MERGE, not clobber. Ship the shipped key to a staging
        path and let install.arm64.sh append+dedup it into the live file.
        See Group "install.arm64.sh append-safe root/.ssh".

      Verification harness already on disk (reuse):
      - (link "/root/compare_devbox_tar.sh" 1) — lists SSH-critical members,
        diffs shipped sshd_config vs live, compares host-key + authorized_keys
        fingerprints, and checks ELF arch. Use it as the acceptance oracle.

* Main Loop :test_tool:
      test_tool = compare_devbox_tar.sh run against the freshly built tarball.
      Run the packer in one shell; run the checker in ANOTHER shell.

      Acceptance oracle (the tarball is host-safe iff ALL are empty/absent):
#+BEGIN_SRC sh
      T=arm64.dev.base.24.04.tar.gz
      # must print NOTHING:
      tar tzf "$T" | grep -E '^(\./)?(etc/ssh/(sshd_config|ssh_config)|etc/ssh/ssh_host_|etc/pam\.d/sshd$|root/\.ssh/(authorized_keys|config))'
      # must still print the payload:
      tar tzf "$T" | grep -E 'usr/sbin/sshd$|usr/bin/ssh$|git-core/git-remote-https$|libcurl-gnutls\.so|etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt$'
      # full acceptance report:
      bash /root/compare_devbox_tar.sh "$PWD/$T"
#+END_SRC

      Loop:
      - (R) run the oracle → identify which forbidden members still leak
      - (E) edit pack.base.arm64.sh list-builder / filters (+ Dockerfile.base)
      - (P) rebuild tarball, re-run oracle + compare_devbox_tar.sh
      - (L) stop when Success criteria all [X]

* ABORT Stop baking secrets into the image (Dockerfile.base)
      IGNORED — wrong premise. `authorized_keys` holds a PUBLIC key, which is
      not a secret; publishing it is harmless. The only real secrets are the
      ssh_host_* PRIVATE keys, and those are already removed by the
      "Patch pack.base.arm64.sh" group. Operator decision: keep root/.ssh/* in
      the tarball. No Dockerfile.base change needed on secret grounds.

      (Residual non-security concern — a plain `tar -C /` OVERWRITES an existing
      host authorized_keys — is handled by the append-safe install group below,
      not here.)

* DONE install.arm64.sh append-safe root/.ssh
      Keep root/.ssh/* in the tarball, but never clobber an existing host key.
      - [X] In pack.base.arm64.sh + pack.arm64.sh, ship the operator key to the
            STAGING path root/.ssh/authorized_keys.devbox (Dockerfile.base COPYs
            both authorized_keys (live in-image) and authorized_keys.devbox
            (staged for tarball)); root/.ssh/config still shipped directly.
      - [X] In install.arm64.sh, after extraction, merge+dedup (awk order-preserve
            de-dup so pre-existing operator keys survive), chmod 600, then remove
            the staging file.
      - [X] Fixed entry.sh `pelse` → `else` typo (broke `docker run -it bash`);
            bash -n entry.sh now passes. (discovered while reproducing the clobber)
      NOTE: verifying a pre-existing operator key (bazhou@nixbase2) survives the
      install and the shipped key (bartuer@…) is ADDED (not substituted) is done
      in the Host-safe validation group's append-safety check.

* Notes
      - The emacs tarball (arm64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz) ALSO ships
        lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 — a separate core-lib clobber risk.
        Out of scope for THIS plan (SSH), but worth a follow-up group if a
        libc-version mismatch is ever observed on-target.
      - Recovery for an already-clobbered box: console/reimage, then restore
        /etc/ssh/sshd_config with the cloud AuthorizedKeysCommand +
        PasswordAuthentication lines, regenerate host keys (ssh-keygen -A),
        and restore the operator's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.
